sourceOfTruth.rule: These are global guardrails. If a symbol or error entry gives a stricter rule, follow the stricter rule.

global: Do not patch from Markdown examples without checking the relevant JSON route and installed DLL.
Do not treat historical version diffs as authoritative.
Do not invent signatures, dependencies, generic arguments, return types, or business logic.
Do not refactor unrelated client code during an upgrade.
Do not copy Core base-class method bodies into client overrides.
Do not edit packages under the NuGet cache.
Do not skip plan or report files.
Do not mark COMPLETED until the report exists.

CS7036: Do not add constructor parameters without passing them to base(...).
Do not forget DI registration and direct new(...) call sites.
CS0305: Do not update only one of interface, implementation, base, and DI registration.
Do not guess the generic argument order.
CS0311: Do not use DTO types when the constraint requires Core model types.
CS0115: Never blindly change override to new.
CS1503: Do not cast away a changed API contract.
NU1201: Do not leave projects on mixed target frameworks after a major Core upgrade.

commands: review final diff for unrelated formatting/refactor churn
successCriteria: The final diff is limited to required package, config, migration, and compile-fix changes.
Every override or constructor change has package evidence recorded.
